item.title: Claude Code API Key Setup (2026): ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, Billing and Login Order
item.description:
Claude Code API key setup means running Claude Code on an Anthropic API key instead of signing in with a claude.ai account. You set the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY variable, and Claude Code sends that key with each request. Anthropic’s Claude Code authentication docs, read 2026-11-19, describe the steps below.

Set up the key

  1. Get a key. Create one in the Claude Console at platform.claude.com. The key belongs to your Console organization.
  2. Export it. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in your shell, for example in your shell profile. Keep the key out of shared scripts.
  3. Start Claude Code. Run claude in your project folder. In interactive mode it asks once whether to use the key. Your answer is remembered.
  4. Check which login is active. Run /status. It marks the login in use and the one that is not.

For the “use this key” choice later, open /config and use the “Use custom API key” toggle. The toggle only shows while ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set. In non-interactive mode (claude -p), the key is always used when it is present, with no prompt.

item.title: Claude Dreaming: Managed Agents Memory Stores and Dreams
item.description:
Claude dreaming is an offline memory pass: Claude rereads past session transcripts and its own memory notes, corrects notes that turned out wrong, merges duplicates, and builds new structures such as a wiki or an index that later sessions can navigate. Anthropic described it in The components of agent memory (November 6, 2026) and ships it in Claude Managed Agents as Dreams, a research-preview API.

This page explains what Anthropic means by agent memory, how memory stores and Dreams work, what the published tests showed (CL-Bench, Pokémon Red, a 420M-token wiki), and how the approach compares with Letta’s dreaming and Hindsight’s background consolidation. Every number comes from Anthropic’s post, its docs or its cookbook, and none of it was reproduced here.

item.title: Claude AI Long-Term Memory: How It Works and Settings
item.description: Claude AI long-term memory is a feature of the Claude apps that saves what you tell it as individual memory topics and uses them in later chats. Paid plans can also search past chats on demand. You control both in Settings > Your Claude (Settings > Memory in the older layout), where you can view and edit each topic, pause memory or reset it. Memory is on by default for Free, Pro, Max and Ultra, on web, desktop and mobile.
